axis_comparison.caveat: 990 pairs each, one corpus, one protocol. The equal-width comparison is between two different cell geometries, not two runs of one cell.
findings: BOTH axes behave the same way: the lower side rises and stops binding. At k=5->10 (M=1) the median rises 0.537->0.778 and 990/990 clear the lower gate, while the joint gate is set entirely by the upper side (upper_only == joint == 98). Same shape as the M axis (M=1->2: 0.537->0.854, joint 127 with upper_only == joint).

The k=5 column here AGREES with the T1 M=1 column but is not bit-identical: median 0.53710 vs 0.53677, joint 359 vs 359, upper_only 363 vs 363. The gate and joint counts are equal; the medians differ by 3e-4, which is the size of a re-draw, because t1b re-draws each service's 20000-flow subsample with the same seed but in a different service order than the T1 run. So this is two implementations agreeing within resampling noise on the same protocol - NOT a reproduction of the identical draw. Do not describe it as "the same numbers".

At EQUAL feature width 1024, refining M does more for the upper side than refining k: joint 127 (M=2,k=5) vs 98 (M=1,k=10). So the two axes are NOT interchangeable at matched dimension - the M direction yields more certifiable pairs at the same width.
axis_comparison.purpose: T1 varied M at k=5 fixed; this run varies k at M=1 fixed. Same object (one-hot over the packed k-prefix symbol law), same protocol (cap 20000/service, seed 20260913, alpha 0.025, michel).

execution_environment.WHY_THIS_MATTERS: These runs executed on the platform-local container, not on server 111 where this project's experiments are configured to run. The corpus sha matches the published one, so the DATA is the same; only the machine differs. If the manuscript adopts the UNCAPPED lower-side convention, these T1/T1b runs must be repeated on server 111 (that host has the memory headroom the local container lacks). Under the capped convention they are usable as they stand.
